content.title: 13 Irish Side Dishes Perfect for St. Patrick's Day
content.text: St. Patrick's Day is just around the corner—a day to celebrate Irish heritage, culture, food, and drink. Everyone's a little luckier, a little happier, and a little more celebratory. It's the Irish touch! There are a number of ways to get into the Irish spirit, but one of the tastiest is to make a tasty spread full of delectable goodies from across the Emerald Isle. We're sharing 15 of our favorite Irish side dishes perfect for St. Patrick's Day—or any day you're looking for a hearty, comforting side dish. Sláinte! Colcannon Dotdash Meredith Food Studios It doesn't get more classic than colcannon, buttery potato mash mixed with cabbage. "I made this for St. Patrick's Day and it was a HUGE hit. Even with my cabbage wary husband and kids," says reviewer Amanda Chapple-Proctor. "It was WONDERFUL." Guinness Beer Cheese Dip Allrecipes Magazine One of Ireland's most beloved exports—Guinness—is the star of the show in this dip. Tasty, cheesy, and good with any type of dipper, this appetizer will be the first to go come St. Paddy's day. Bonus points if it's made with Irish cheese. "I make this almost every time we have a party or gathering to go to," shared Allrecipes user Caitlin. "It’s wonderful." Mashed Peas Allrecipes Magazine Mashed Peas, otherwise known as mushy peas, is a vibrant and tasty addition to any Irish spread. Commonly found on pub menus, this classic side dish is so tasty, even your picky eaters are sure to enjoy. This particular recipe has some additional add-ins like fresh mint, brown sugar, and green onions that make it special. "Made for St. Paddy's Day dinner and these were AWESOME," shared one Allrecipes member. "Fresh mint is the secret ingredient that wow, takes this over the top! After working my arm off trying to mash, I used my immersion blender - which did the trick! Would and will absolutely make again!" Irish Brown Bread Allrecipes / Christine Ma Brown bread is a hearty, versatile bread that's perfect for sopping up sauces, or eating plain. Serve with a hearty swipe of good Irish butter and enjoy. "This is a wonderful, easy to make bread that is so close to the bread I fell in love with in Ireland," shared Allrecipes member Asabo. "Made a loaf for my daughter’s friend from Ireland who is currently studying here. She also gave it high praise!" Irish Boxty Photographer: Jason Donnelly Boxty is a traditional Irish potato pancake made with leftover mashed potato and grated raw potato. An old Irish rhyme goes: "Boxty on the griddle, boxty on the pan; if you can't make boxty, you'll never get a man." Allrecipes member Brooke Elizabeth, who shared this recipe, said their family has been making this delicious recipe for years! "A delightful meal accompaniment," said one reviewer. "I did add some sweet onion and a dash of cayenne—my own preference. Very easy to make and went over well with the family. I'll make this again." Irish Beer Cheese Puffs ALLRECIPES/ BAHAREH NAITI Chef John, who shared this recipe, says it's "by no means an authentic Irish recipe, I do use Irish beer, Irish butter, and sharp Irish Cheddar," the result is easy, cheesy puffs that are perfect for entertaining. Delicious to eat alone or with the cheese spread included in the recipe. "Hands down! Best! Unique appetizer or side dish I have tried in a while," raved one reviewer. "Absolutely delicious!! And I am NOT a baker! While my “puffs” turned out closer to a cookie/cookie texture- they were mind-blowing good!" Irish Potato Farls Dotdash Meredith Food Studios Allrecipes own Northern Irish delegate, Ita, shared this recipe for Irish Potato Farls. She said, "the word farl originates from the Gaelic word fardel meaning four parts. These potato griddle breads can be made with leftover mashed potatoes if you have them. Serve hot with a little butter and salt or fry them alongside soda bread as part of an Ulster Fry." "This is very close to my great-grandmother's recipe," shared one Allrecipes user. "I use an Iron Skillet over a med-high heat and that works best for me. Thank you for this recipe and a touch of Ireland!" Creamed Cabbage MrsMunch Creamed cabbage with crispy crumbled bacon is a yummy recipe for St. Patrick's Day! "My family loved this dish," said Allrecipes member Cindy O. "I followed the recipe exactly, and when I make it again I won't change a thing. For cabbage lovers, this is a great option." Irish Soda Bread Photographer: Jason Donnelly Soda bread is perfect for breakfast, lunch, or dinner—making it the most versatile dish on this list. One taste and you'll want to make it again and again. Plus, this recipe has over 1,000 5-star ratings! "Could not get more compliments on this recipe," said an Allrecipes user. "What’s better is how easy it is. Don’t forget to get the real Irish butter to go with it. Pop it in a the microwave a few seconds and add that butter and yummmmy!" Irish Champ Grocery Addict Irish champ is similar to colcannon, but is made by blending green onions or scallions with creamy mashed potatoes. It's great on its own or served steaming hot with extra butter on top. It's also a perfect side dish for good quality sausages. "My mouth is watering just thinking about it," raved Frank San Pietro, Allrecipes member. "So creamy and flavorful." Cabbage Fritters Dotdash Meredith Food Studios This may be your new favorite way to eat cabbage. Sweet, salty, and oh-so comforting. The tangy feta dill dip provides a cool contrast. "We love recipes that includes lots of fresh vegetables and this recipe turned out to be one of our favorites," said one Allrecipes members. "We're not vegans or vegetarians but this recipe is a nice change of pace and we will have it often!" Potato Rolls Dotdash Meredith Food Studios While you're making potatoes for any of the recipes above, make a few extra to enjoy these delicious potato rolls. "This is my all time favorite recipe," said one Allrecipes reviewer. "Before I throw them in the oven though I brush them with an egg wash and sprinkle sea salt on top. One of my friends and family's most requested recipes!" Beer Bread Dotdash Meredith Food Studios Beer Bread is a quick bread to make to accompany any beef dish. The type of beer you use will change the taste. Serve topped with butter or cheese spread. "I make this whenever I make soup—any soup," said Cheryl B. "It’s our family fave! Usually I add a cup of shredded cheddar and a teaspoon of garlic powder to the batter, and brush melted butter on the hot loaf before taking it out of the pan to cool. Always delish!"
